claim: NAS-Bench-101 is the first public tabular architecture dataset for NAS research, built by reducing a cell-based search space via graph isomorphism to 423,000 unique convolutional architectures, each trained and evaluated multiple times on CIFAR-10.
stance_target: existence and construction of the canonical tabular NAS benchmark named in question THREE
scope_conditions: CIFAR-10 image classification, cell-based convolutional search space
quoted_support: "we carefully constructed a compact, yet expressive, search space, exploiting graph isomorphisms to identify 423k unique convolutional architectures. We trained and evaluated all of these architectures multiple times on CIFAR-10 and compiled the results into a large dataset of over 5 million trained models."

claim: NAS-Bench-101 was created explicitly to solve a reproducibility crisis in NAS: prior methods demanded tremendous compute, making experiments hard to reproduce and creating a barrier to entry for researchers without large-scale compute access.
stance_target: the methodological need for cheap, reproducible, lookup-based evaluation in NAS papers (relevant to whether a small quantized-LLM NAS paper can be evaluated cheaply and reproducibly)
scope_conditions: framed as a general problem with NAS research circa 2019
quoted_support: "Recent advances in neural architecture search (NAS) demand tremendous computational resources, which makes it difficult to reproduce experiments and imposes a barrier-to-entry to researchers without access to large-scale computation. We aim to ameliorate these problems by introducing NAS-Bench-101."

claim: The NAS-Bench-101 paper itself validates the dataset's utility by benchmarking a range of architecture optimization algorithms against it, establishing the precedent that any new architecture-search method (including an LLM proposer) should be validated by querying this same lookup table rather than training new models from scratch.
stance_target: methodology standard for tabular-benchmark evaluation named in question THREE
scope_conditions: CIFAR-10 cell-based search space, algorithms available circa 2019 (e.g. random search, evolution, RL, Bayesian optimization)
quoted_support: "This allows researchers to evaluate the quality of a diverse range of models in milliseconds by querying the pre-computed dataset. We demonstrate its utility by analyzing the dataset as a whole and by benchmarking a range of architecture optimization algorithms."
